title: Comparison isomorphism of compact-support candidates along a refinement
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $c_i=(j_i,\bar f_i)$, $i=1,2$, be objects of the compactification category $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$, with $j_i:X\hookrightarrow\overline X_i$ an open immersion and $\bar f_i:\overline X_i\to Y$ proper, and let $u:c_1\to c_2$ be a refinement [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]: a proper $Y$-morphism $u:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ (so $\bar f_2\circ u=\bar f_1$) with $u\circ j_1=j_2$. Write $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $D^{+}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the derived category, and its bounded-below part, of sheaves of $A$-modules on the small pro-etale site of a scheme $T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], $D^{+}(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for the bounded-below derived category of etale sheaves of $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and $\nu_T^*$ for the inverse image along the comparison morphism of sites $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Write $Rf_{!,n}^{c_i}=R\bar f_{i*,n}\,j_{i!}:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the compact-support candidates [def-weil-compact-support-candidate], composed from the derived direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and the extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] (exact on sheaves, applied degreewise). Let $(K,L,\alpha)$ be an object of the category $\mathcal D^{+}_{\mathrm{et}}(X,A)$ of complexes coming from the etale site [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]: $K\in D^{+}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $L\in D^{+}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\alpha:\nu_X^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, an etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].

(a) *The proper-open isomorphism at $(K,L,\alpha)$.* The schemes $\overline X_1,\overline X_2$ are of finite type over $K_0$ (proper over $Y$, which is of finite type over $K_0$), hence Noetherian, and $u$ is proper with $u\circ j_1=j_2$; so the proper-open comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale] gives its canonical isomorphism $\alpha_u(L):j_{2!}\nu_X^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{*,n}\,j_{1!}\nu_X^*L$ in $D(\overline X_{2,\mathrm{proet}},A)$. (That lemma uses the derived direct image of the proper-base-change chapter [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and the extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero]; the former is the same construction, by a K-injective resolution, as [def-weil-derived-direct-image] at finite level.) Transport it along the witness:
$$
 \alpha_u(K,L,\alpha)=Ru_{*,n}j_{1!}(\alpha)\circ\alpha_u(L)\circ j_{2!}(\alpha)^{-1}:\ j_{2!}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ru_{*,n}\,j_{1!}K .
$$
When $K=\nu_X^*L$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ this is $\alpha_u(L)$.

(b) *The comparison along $u$.* The comparison isomorphism along $u$ at $(K,L,\alpha)$ is the composite
$$
 \theta_u(K,L,\alpha):
 Rf_{!,n}^{c_1}K=R\bar f_{1*,n}\,j_{1!}K
 \xrightarrow{\ c_{\bar f_2,u}(j_{1!}K)\ }
 R\bar f_{2*,n}\,Ru_{*,n}\,j_{1!}K
 \xrightarrow{\ R\bar f_{2*,n}(\alpha_u(K,L,\alpha)^{-1})\ }
 R\bar f_{2*,n}\,j_{2!}K=Rf_{!,n}^{c_2}K,
$$
where $c_{\bar f_2,u}:R(\bar f_2\circ u)_{*,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar f_{2*,n}\circ Ru_{*,n}$ is the composition isomorphism of derived direct images at finite level [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition, part 1], applied to $\bar f_1=\bar f_2\circ u$. It is a morphism of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and, as a composite of two isomorphisms, an isomorphism. It is defined on the object $(K,L,\alpha)$, not on $K$ alone: the witness enters through (a).

Not part of this definition: that $\theta_u$ is natural with respect to the morphisms of $\mathcal D^{+}_{\mathrm{et}}(X,A)$ (so that it is a natural isomorphism $Rf^{c_1}_{!,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^{c_2}_{!,n}$ of functors on $\mathcal D^{+}_{\mathrm{et}}(X,A)$), that it does not depend on the witness, that it is the identity for the identity refinement, and that $\theta_{v\circ u}=\theta_v\circ\theta_u$. These are properties, asserted with the compactification coherence (node prop-compactification-coherence-detailed, not cited as a dependency since it is stated in terms of this comparison); the proper-open comparison as stated gives no naturality in $L$, so the naturality needs an argument of its own there.

split_report.summary: Checked the definition against its source (master blueprint prop-compactification-coherence.md, statement and proof steps 1-2; no slopmaster2 counterpart file) and against the nodes it uses. Every notion is now a statement dependency: added def-weil-pbc-proetale-site and def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules (D(T_proet,A), D^+), def-weil-pbc-derived-categories (D^+(T_et,A)), def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism (nu_T^*) and def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness (the witness alpha), which the statement used without citing; field, Noetherian scheme (AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian, with LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian), isomorphism and composite in a category are Mathlib notions. No new node was needed. Corrected the statement: the old text applied the proper-open comparison to K as if K were nu_X^*L; the lemma only gives an isomorphism for nu_X^*L, so the definition now transports it along the witness alpha (part (a)), which is where the witness enters. The old text also asserted that theta_u is natural in (K,L,alpha); the cited lemma states no naturality in L and morphisms of D^+_et are arbitrary morphisms of D(X_proet,A), so naturality is not a consequence of the definition: it is now listed, with independence of the witness and the identity and composition laws, as a property not part of the definition. Lean: no Lean on either branch for this node. The source repository (slopmaster2) has a different comparison, AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusComparison (WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Etale/Derived/LowerShriekComparison.lean, line 148): it is on the etale site, not the pro-etale site; it requires the square X -> c.Z, X -> d.Z over r.hom to be cartesian (r.hom^{-1}(X)=X); and it runs from the coarser compactification d to the finer c (Rf_!(d) -> Rf_!(c), built from the unit of q^* -| Rq_*, the inverse of the base change for j_!, and the composition of pushforwards), whereas theta_u runs from the finer c_1 to the coarser c_2 and needs no cartesian hypothesis, since the proper-open comparison holds for any refinement (j_1(X) is open and closed in u^{-1}(j_2(X)), being a section of the proper map u over j_2(X)); that the Lean comparison is an isomorphism is not proved there.
